appraisal_events.evidence: il y eut un mouvement de curiosité et de déférence quand il entra... j'étais peut-être seul à savoir qu'il avait été entretenu par M. de Charlus, puis par Saint-Loup et en même temps par un ami de Saint-Loup
appraisal_events.explanation: Society greets Morel with curiosity and deference because of his morally weighty courtroom testimony, but the narrator's exclusive private knowledge that Morel had been a kept man undercuts this esteem, making the elevation ironic rather than narrator-endorsed.

appraisal_events.evidence: il avait fait... une apparition de grand homme... [ses ouvrages] donnaient aux jeunes gens et à beaucoup de femmes du monde l'impression d'une hauteur intellectuelle peu commune, d'une sorte de génie... ouvrages sans originalité
appraisal_events.explanation: Having broken cleanly with the declining circle where he once cut a poor figure, Bloch reappears in a new society celebrated as a man of genius; the narrator immediately qualifies this reputation as resting on unoriginal, sophistical work, marking the elevation as ironic.

status_effects.explanation: Within the scene Morel visibly gains curiosity and deference from the assembled company, a real if hollow elevation given what the narrator alone knows about his past dependence on Charlus and Saint-Loup.
Bloch's local standing rises sharply as he is received in his new milieu as a man of talent and near-genius, his earlier mediocre social position forgotten by those who never knew it.

ambiguities: Both elevations (Morel, Bloch) are staged as sincere social esteem on the surface but are immediately reframed by the narrator's privileged knowledge or judgment as unfounded, so the positive polarity should be read as socially real but epistemically hollow rather than narrator-endorsed.

The passage also sketches a parallel case of social forgetting distorting reputations (a young lord's account inverting Swann's and Forcheville's relative standing, contested by the duchesse de Guermantes and others), but this thread is more diffuse and secondary to the two focal, sustained reputational reversals (Morel, Bloch) selected here.
